subject: [SignalWorks] Split-horizon resolver misroutes causing latency & 502s
messages:
From: Jane Doe <jane.doe@signalworks.com>
To: support@redwood.ai; sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: infra@signalworks.com
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 15:34:00 -0800
Subject: [URGENT] Spike in storefront latency and intermittent 502s (region: us-west)

Hi team,

We started seeing a spike in latency and intermittent 502s hitting our customer storefronts around 14:20 PST. The errors are inconsistent — roughly 18–25% of requests fail or time out, latency spikes to 1.2–2.5s for otherwise simple generation requests. This is impacting our checkout flow.

We collected tcpdump traces and a basic DNS trace and attached them (service-logs-20261114.zip, dns-trace-20261114.txt). Initial look shows some clients resolving model API endpoints to an unexpected edge IP that routes through a proxy cluster with high tail latency.

Can you triage ASAP and advise an ETA? We have a Black Friday test next week so this is high priority.

Thanks,
Jane
Ops Lead, SignalWorks
attachments: service-logs-20261114.zip, dns-trace-20261114.txt
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@signalworks.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 15:48:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: [URGENT] Spike in storefront latency and intermittent 502s (region: us-west)

Jane — thanks for the alert and the traces. We’ve opened INC-8742 and started a triage. Initial hypothesis: split-horizon resolver mismatch (some resolvers returning older delegated NS records) causing a subset of client IPs to hit an older proxy fleet that has an overloaded path.

Grace and Marissa are pulling logs for the affected edge IPs now. Can you confirm if SignalWorks is using any private DNS forwarding or custom resolvers in us-west? That would help narrow down delegation issues.

We’ll update within 30 minutes.

— Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Customer Escalations, Redwood Inference
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 16:10:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: [URGENT] Spike in storefront latency and intermittent 502s (region: us-west)

Triage update:
- Observed backend p50/p95/p99 increases for requests routed via edgeIP 54.186.33.21 and 54.186.33.22. 502 rate correlates with connections hitting proxy-cluster-old-03.
- Resolver logs show mixed answers for model-api.signalworks.redwood.ai: some resolvers return 54.186.33.21 (old proxy), others return 18.204.12.99 (new proxy). TTLs are low but delegation changed yesterday during a rollout.
- No CPU/memory pressure on the runtime nodes for the new proxy cluster; latency appears localized to the old proxy cluster and an external firewall appliance in that path exhibiting queueing.

Action items I’m running now:
1) Ask infra to temporarily blackhole the old proxy VIP for client-facing prefixes (will force failover to the healthy proxy cluster).
2) Request SignalWorks confirm any on-prem DNS caches or forwarders (low TTLs could still be cached locally).
3) Collect additional packet captures across affected prefixes.

Attaching resolver-config-diff.patch with the delegation changes we pushed.

— Grace
Grace O'Connor
Edge Reliability, Redwood Inference
attachments: resolver-config-diff.patch
From: infra@signalworks.com
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai; sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: [URGENT] Spike in storefront latency and intermittent 502s (region: us-west)

Grace, Sergio — we do have a pair of recursive resolvers behind a firewall appliance in our us-west colo. They cache NS records for delegated zones for up to 300s despite low TTLs from your authoritative servers — the appliance is running a snapshot config that pins delegation data after a scheduled maintenance.

We can flush the caches but the appliance needs a config change and a restart window (~90s). We’re ready to do that on your go-ahead.

— SignalWorks Infra

Thanks — perform the cache flush and restart. We will simultaneously coordinate a targeted VIP withdrawal for the old proxy VIPs (canary blackhole) to force clients to the healthy cluster.

Vivek — FYI this is escalating toward exec attention from the customer; if the cache flush + VIP withdrawal does not reduce error rates within 10 minutes we should consider an emergency failover and a customer credit conversation.

— Marissa
Sr. Account Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai; sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai; grace_oconnor@redwood.ai; monica_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: jane.doe@signalworks.com
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 19:12:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: [URGENT] Spike in storefront latency and intermittent 502s (region: us-west) — Post-mortem summary and next steps

Final update: the remediation (SignalWorks cache flush + our targeted blackhole of old proxy VIPs) reduced error rates from ~20% -> <0.5% and p99 dropped from 2.5s -> 160ms within 6 minutes.

Root cause: a split-horizon resolver scenario combined with a deployment that updated NS delegation yesterday. A subset of SignalWorks' on-prem resolvers continued returning the pre-rollout delegated NS set; traffic for those clients reached a legacy proxy cluster that had an overloaded upstream firewall appliance. The overloaded path produced queueing and 502s.

Customer impact: intermittent transaction failures for US-west storefronts over ~55 minutes; high severity for SignalWorks during a critical load test.

Follow-ups / action items:
- Run an automated DNS delegations consistency check in our rollout pipeline. (Owner: Grace)
- Add a pre-cutover advisory to customers when delegation changes occur for delegated subdomains. (Owner: Marissa)
- Improve telemetry to surface resolver-level divergence (owner: Monica).
- Offer SignalWorks a one-time service credit; Marissa to lead.

Attachments: service-logs-20261114.zip, dns-trace-20261114.txt included in the incident record. Confluence summary: https://redwood.ai/confluence/INC-8742-signalworks

— Vivek
VP, Customer Success, Redwood Inference
